narr: A longwave trough moved out of the Intermountain West into the Southern Plains on April 20th, which reinforced a weak cold front southeast into East Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana during the late afternoon through the evening into the early morning hours of the 21st. Strong heating ahead of the front as well as ample moisture enhanced instability ahead of the front, with large scale forcing sufficient along and ahead of the front/trough for the development of scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. While no severe weather was observed, the very moist atmospheric environment as well as the storm motion which allowed for thunderstorms to move repeatedly over the same areas did result in localized flash flooding over portions of Caddo Parish (including the city of Shreveport) in Northwest Louisiana during the evening hours, where rainfall totals ranged from 1-3 inches in a short period of time.
